_meta.purpose: Phase 3 de-risk labelled study set: REAL central-bank / macro prose snippets with hand-assigned forecast-relevant direction labels.
_meta.provenance: All 'text' fields are VERBATIM sentences copied from the cloned real Track 2 corpus at /home/matt/ozmadev/ocelot/.bigtmp/track2/units/<unit>/text/<file>. Extracted via extract_snippets.py, then the load-bearing sentence(s) selected by hand. No paraphrase; a few are lightly trimmed to the load-bearing clause (marked trim=true).
_meta.label_rubric: Direction = the forecast-relevant move in the unit's rate/FX TARGET implied by the text's forward-guidance/regime tone, from a forecaster's seat. up = hawkish/tightening/restrictive/less-easing-than-priced (rates band UP). down = dovish/easing/accommodative/backstop/less-tightening-than-priced (rates band DOWN). none = neutral, on-hold with balanced risks, or pure data with no directional policy implication. Anchored on the unit name + card [text].notes + card [targets], NOT on the surface action verb. THE ACTION VERB IS OFTEN A TRAP (a cut delivered with a hawkish path -> up).
_meta.labeller: phase3-derisk (single annotator; labels anchored to organizer unit intent)

snippets.text: In considering the extent and timing of additional adjustments to the target range for the federal funds rate, the Committee will carefully assess incoming data, the evolving outlook, and the balance of risks.
snippets.note: TRAP: same meeting delivered a 25bp CUT, but the load-bearing signal is the shallower forward path ('extent and timing... carefully assess') vs the easing narrative -> 2Y up. Unit named hawkish-cut.

snippets.text: In support of its goals, the Committee decided to lower the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point to 4-1/4 to 4-1/2 percent.
snippets.note: Isolated, this SENTENCE reads dovish (a cut). Included to test whether the typer over-weights the action verb. Sentence-level direction=down; unit-level=up (context).

snippets.text: The all items index rose 2.7 percent for the 12 months ending November, after rising 2.6 percent over the 12 months ending October.
snippets.note: CPI reaccelerating (2.6->2.7) = firmer inflation = hawkish tilt for rates. Data release; direction must be read from the number-direction.

snippets.text: The Committee anticipates that it will be appropriate to raise the target range for the federal funds rate when it has seen some further improvement in the labor market and is reasonably confident that inflation will move back to its 2 percent objective over the medium term.
snippets.note: Telegraphing liftoff (first hike). Clear hawkish forward guidance.

snippets.text: In determining whether it will be appropriate to raise the target range at its next meeting, the Committee will assess progress--both realized and expected--toward its objectives of maximum employment and 2 percent inflation.
snippets.note: 'at its next meeting' = strengthened liftoff signal; hawkish.

snippets.text: The Committee anticipates that it will be appropriate to raise the target range for the federal funds rate when it has seen further improvement in the labor market and is reasonably confident that inflation will move back to its 2 percent objective over the medium term.
snippets.note: 'patient' dropped -> hike getting closer; hawkish.

snippets.text: Consistent with its previous statement, the Committee judges that an increase in the target range for the federal funds rate remains unlikely at the April FOMC meeting.
snippets.note: TRAP: dovish qualifier ('increase... remains unlikely at April') tempering the hawkish drift. Sentence-level = down/dovish. Tests negation handling.

snippets.text: However, if incoming information indicates faster progress toward the Committee's employment and inflation objectives than the Committee now expects, then increases in the target range for the federal funds rate are likely to occur sooner than currently anticipated.
snippets.note: Conditional hawkish; 'increases... sooner'.

snippets.text: Conversely, if progress proves slower than expected, then increases in the target range are likely to occur later than currently anticipated.
snippets.note: Conditional dovish; symmetric to s08. Tests that 'increases' word alone doesn't force up.

snippets.text: In light of the implications of global developments for the economic outlook as well as muted inflation pressures, the Committee decided to lower the target range for the federal funds rate to 1-1/2 to 1-3/4 percent.
snippets.note: The 'third cut' mid-cycle easing; dovish action AND dovish context align here.

snippets.text: The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to raise its target for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 5-1/4 percent.
snippets.note: A hike (the last of the cycle before the pause). Action=up. Unit is 'pause' but this statement itself is the hike.

snippets.text: Recent indicators suggest that economic growth is moderating from its quite strong pace earlier this year, partly reflecting a gradual cooling of the housing market and the lagged effects of increases in interest rates and energy prices.
snippets.note: TRAP: contains 'increases in interest rates' but the SIGNAL is growth moderating/cooling -> the coming pause -> dovish tilt. Tests that lexical 'increases' != hawkish.

snippets.text: With underlying inflation still expected to be relatively low, the Committee believes that policy accommodation can be removed at a pace that is likely to be measured.
snippets.note: 'accommodation can be removed at a measured pace' = gradual tightening. Hawkish but softened. Classic 'measured' guidance.

snippets.text: In these circumstances, the Committee believes that policy accommodation can be maintained for a considerable period.
snippets.note: 'accommodation... for a considerable period' = commitment to stay easy = dovish/low-for-long.

snippets.text: The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to keep its target for the federal funds rate at 1 percent.
snippets.note: On hold, no directional guidance in this sentence. Neutral.

snippets.text: If incoming information broadly supports the Committee's expectation of ongoing improvement in labor market conditions and inflation moving back toward its longer-run objective, the Committee will likely reduce the pace of asset purchases in further measured steps at future meetings.
snippets.note: TAPER = reduce QE = tightening of policy stance = hawkish for rates. Note the verb is 'reduce' (usually dovish-adjacent) but reducing PURCHASES is hawkish. Hard case.

snippets.text: The Committee now anticipates that it likely will be appropriate to maintain the current target range for the federal funds rate well past the time that the unemployment rate declines below 6-1/2 percent, especially if projected inflation continues to run below the Committee's 2 percent longer-run goal.
snippets.note: Dovish forward guidance ('lower for longer') offsetting the taper. Same statement, opposite-signed sentence.

snippets.text: At its most recent meeting, the Committee made clear that it is prepared to increase or reduce the pace of its asset purchases to ensure that the stance of monetary policy remains appropriate as the outlook for the labor market or inflation changes.
snippets.note: The 'taper tantrum' trigger testimony: signalling purchases could be reduced -> markets sold off, yields up. Directionally hawkish (the tapering risk).

snippets.text: A premature tightening of monetary policy could lead interest rates to rise temporarily but would also carry a substantial risk of slowing or ending the economic recovery and causing inflation to fall further.
snippets.note: TRAP: contains 'tightening' and 'interest rates to rise' but the CLAIM is a warning AGAINST premature tightening = dovish reassurance. Tests negation/framing.

snippets.text: In determining the extent of additional policy firming that may be appropriate to return inflation to 2 percent over time, the Committee will take into account the cumulative tightening of monetary policy, the lags with which monetary policy affects economic activity and inflation.
snippets.note: 'additional policy firming' + 'higher for longer' regime -> hawkish.

snippets.text: In support of these goals, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 5-1/4 to 5-1/2 percent.
snippets.note: TRAP: action = 'maintain' (looks neutral) but in the higher-for-longer regime the hold WITH firming bias is hawkish. Sentence in isolation reads none; unit intent up. Labeled up per rubric anchor on unit intent + accompanying firming language.

snippets.text: Within our mandate, the ECB is ready to do whatever it takes to preserve the euro. And believe me, it will be enough.
snippets.note: THE pivotal easing/backstop signal of the era -> peripheral yields collapsed, EUR stabilized (risk-on, rate-relief). Dovish. CONTAINS ZERO directional-cue vocabulary. The lexicon-killer.

snippets.text: To the extent that the size of these sovereign premia hampers the functioning of the monetary policy transmission channel, they come within our mandate.
snippets.note: Justification for intervention (OMT precursor) = dovish backstop. Again no cue vocabulary.

snippets.text: Second, as the Governing Council concluded that the conditions underlying our forward guidance have been satisfied, we intend to raise the key ECB interest rates by 25 basis points at our July monetary policy meeting.
snippets.note: Explicit ECB hike telegraph; hawkish.

snippets.text: And fourth, beyond September, based on our current assessment, we anticipate that a gradual but sustained path of further increases in interest rates will be appropriate.
snippets.note: 'sustained path of further increases' -> hawkish.

snippets.text: If the medium-term inflation outlook persists or deteriorates, a larger increment will be appropriate at our September meeting.
snippets.note: Conditional escalation ('larger increment') -> hawkish.

snippets.text: The Committee judges that some further gradual increases in the target range for the federal funds rate will be consistent with sustained expansion of economic activity, strong labor market conditions, and inflation near the Committee's symmetric 2 percent objective over the medium term.
snippets.note: Dec 2018 hawkish hold-the-path language (pre-pivot). 'further gradual increases' -> hawkish. (The 2019 pivot came LATER; this doc is the hawkish setup.)

snippets.text: In view of realized and expected labor market conditions and inflation, the Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 2-1/4 to 2-1/2 percent.
snippets.note: The Dec 2018 hike itself; action=up, hawkish.

snippets.text: The Committee does not expect it will be appropriate to reduce the target range until it has gained greater confidence that inflation is moving sustainably toward 2 percent.
snippets.note: Pre-cut conditioning: 'reduce... until greater confidence' -> the easing is coming = dovish setup. TRAP: identical wording to s31 (time-has-come) but different unit.

snippets.text: Inflation has eased over the past year but remains somewhat elevated.
snippets.note: 'inflation has eased' softening -> dovish tilt toward the cut.

snippets.text: The Committee does not expect it will be appropriate to reduce the target range until it has gained greater confidence that inflation is moving sustainably toward 2 percent.
snippets.note: Same sentence as s29, different unit -> exposes the LIMIT of sentence-only typing: identical text, and here still dovish setup. Direction is stable across the two here (both down), but see s21/s02 for cases where identical actions differ by context.

snippets.text: These actions, which together will increase the Committee's holdings of longer-term securities by about $85 billion each month through the end of the year, should put downward pressure on longer-term interest rates, support mortgage markets, and help to make broader financial conditions more accommodative.
snippets.note: QE expansion -> 'downward pressure on longer-term interest rates' = dovish. NOTE: verb 'increase' (holdings) but effect is dovish. Hard case mirror of taper (s16).

snippets.text: The Committee continues to anticipate that it likely will be appropriate to maintain the current target range for the federal funds rate for a considerable time after the asset purchase program ends, especially if projected inflation continues to run below the Committee's 2 percent longer-run goal.
snippets.note: 'maintain... for a considerable time' low-for-long -> dovish forward guidance.

snippets.text: In light of the cumulative progress toward maximum employment and the improvement in the outlook for labor market conditions since the inception of the current asset purchase program, the Committee decided to make a further measured reduction in the pace of its asset purchases.
snippets.note: Continued taper ('reduction in the pace of asset purchases') -> hawkish stance shift. Verb 'reduction' again NOT dovish.

snippets.text: In support of these goals, the Committee decided to raise the target range for the federal funds rate to 1-1/2 to 1-3/4 percent and anticipates that ongoing increases in the target range will be appropriate.
snippets.note: 75bp hike + 'ongoing increases' -> strongly hawkish.

snippets.text: The Committee expects that further gradual increases in the target range for the federal funds rate will be consistent with sustained expansion of economic activity, strong labor market conditions, and inflation near the Committee's symmetric 2 percent objective over the medium term.
snippets.note: Hawkish forward guidance ('further gradual increases').

snippets.text: In view of realized and expected labor market conditions and inflation, the Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 2 to 2-1/4 percent.
snippets.note: Action = maintain, this sentence in isolation is neutral. Labeled none (sentence-level).

snippets.text: The Committee anticipates that ongoing increases in the target range will be appropriate in order to attain a stance of monetary policy that is sufficiently restrictive to return inflation to 2 percent over time.
snippets.note: 'ongoing increases... sufficiently restrictive' -> hawkish (this is the Feb-2023 setup BEFORE the SVB shock reversed the path).

snippets.text: SVB Financial Group Announces Proposed Offerings of Common Stock and Mandatory Convertible Preferred Stock. Additionally, earlier today, SVB completed the sale of substantially all of its available for sale securities portfolio.
snippets.note: SHOCK signal: emergency capital raise + fire-sale of the securities book -> bank-run trigger -> flight-to-quality, front-end yields COLLAPSED (dovish for rates). ZERO monetary-policy vocabulary; a corporate filing. Extreme lexicon-killer / tail-from-text case (trim=true).

snippets.text: To support continued progress toward maximum employment and price stability, the Committee expects that a highly accommodative stance of monetary policy will remain appropriate for a considerable time after the asset purchase program ends and the economic recovery strengthens.
snippets.note: 'highly accommodative... for a considerable time' -> dovish. (The taper WARNING/shock came later in 2013.)

snippets.text: In light of inflation developments and the further improvement in the labor market, the Committee decided to reduce the monthly pace of its net asset purchases by $20 billion for Treasury securities and $10 billion for agency mortgage-backed securities.
snippets.note: Accelerated taper -> hawkish. Verb 'reduce' (purchases) = hawkish, again the anti-lexical case.

snippets.text: The Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 1-1/2 to 1-3/4 percent.
snippets.note: Jan 2020 hold, pre-COVID, balanced. Neutral.

snippets.text: Market-based measures of inflation compensation remain low; survey-based measures of longer-term inflation expectations are little changed.
snippets.note: Descriptive, no policy direction. Neutral.

snippets.text: In these circumstances, the Committee's predominant policy concern remains the risk that inflation will fail to moderate as expected.
snippets.note: Hawkish bias ('predominant concern... inflation') even while on hold -> tightening tilt.

snippets.text: The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to keep its target for the federal funds rate at 5-1/4 percent.
snippets.note: On hold, this sentence neutral.

snippets.text: CFTC Commitments of Traders — JAPANESE YEN (CME). Weekly Tuesday positions; noncommercial net short position deeply negative and extending through mid-2007.
snippets.note: Record JPY carry short-positioning = crowded carry trade -> tail risk of violent JPY appreciation (yen up = a 'down' move in USDJPY). Tabular positioning data, no prose cue words. Direction read from position extremity, not language (trim=true).

snippets.text: The Committee does not expect it will be appropriate to reduce the target range until it has gained greater confidence that inflation is moving sustainably toward 2 percent.
snippets.note: 'greater confidence' framing = the pre-cut condition -> dovish path forming. Namesake sentence of the unit.

snippets.text: The Committee expects that, with appropriate policy accommodation, economic growth will pick up from its recent pace and the unemployment rate will gradually decline toward levels the Committee judges consistent with its dual mandate.
snippets.note: Boilerplate outlook, no directional policy signal in isolation. Neutral. Tests over-firing on generic 'accommodation'.

snippets.text: The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to raise its target for the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to 1-1/4 percent.
snippets.note: Start of the 2004 hiking cycle; action=up, hawkish.

snippets.text: In addition, the Committee will continue reducing its holdings of Treasury securities and agency debt and agency mortgage-backed securities, as described in the Plans for Reducing the Size of the Federal Reserve's Balance Sheet that were issued in May.
snippets.note: Quantitative tightening (balance-sheet runoff) -> hawkish. Verb 'reducing' = hawkish here.

snippets.text: The Committee perceives that the upside and downside risks to the attainment of sustainable growth for the next few quarters are roughly equal.
snippets.note: Explicitly balanced risks -> neutral.

snippets.text: The Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U) rose 0.6 percent in August on a seasonally adjusted basis, after increasing 0.2 percent in July, the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reported today.
snippets.note: Hot CPI print (0.6% m/m, up from 0.2% in July, gasoline-driven) -> hawkish for rates. Data release read from the number-direction, not policy vocabulary.
